en: Certain bamboo species are the fastest-growing plants on Earth, capable of growing up to 91 centimeters in a single day.
A mantis shrimp's claw strikes so incredibly fast that it boils the surrounding water and creates a brief flash of light.
The common wombat is the only known animal that produces cube-shaped feces to prevent its droppings from rolling away.
Your stomach must generate a completely new mucus lining every three to four days to prevent its own acids from digesting it.
The human nose is incredibly sensitive and can distinguish and remember over one trillion different individual scents.
Periodical cicada nymphs spend up to 17 years living underground feeding on tree roots before finally emerging as flying adults.
Adult mayflies lack functional mouthparts and live for only 24 hours, giving them one of the shortest adult lifespans in nature.
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor but provide a habitat for twenty-five percent of all marine species.
Underground fungal networks called mycelium connect forest trees, allowing them to share water, nutrients, and even chemical warning signals.
Contrary to popular myth, a camel's hump stores thick fat for energy rather than liquid water to survive harsh deserts.
The Mexican axolotl possesses an amazing ability to fully regenerate its brain, spinal cord, heart, and limbs multiple times.
A single human sneeze can expel up to 40,000 droplets traveling at speeds of 100 miles per hour.
